newsitem.title: FRANCE: True North's FCB says Publicis break-up beneficial.
newsitem.headline: True North's FCB says Publicis break-up beneficial.

text.p: Advertising agency Foote Cone & Belding is in a stronger position to win global accounts since its parent company, True North Communications, ended its alliance with France's Publicis ad group earlier this year, an FCB executive said.

"Dissolving the alliance gave us back ownership of the network," Geoff Thompson, worldwide creative director for FCB, told Reuters in an interview at the International Advertising Festival here. "Publicis was in charge of the joint venture in Europe," Thompson explained.

In the case of a U.S.-based client of FCB with operations around the world, that meant having FCB handle its advertising in all markets outside of Europe, while Publicis ran the client's European advertising affairs. The split did not create problems in the actual handling of clients' ad accounts, but did create a public perception of problems and confusion, Thompson said.

"If you ever asked any of the FCB or Publicis clients, it was never a problem," he said. "But clients looking at us for a global consolidation (of their advertising accounts) saw all these problems mentioned in the press."
Global consolidation accounts for which FCB pitched and lost out on during the alliance with Publicis included those for Bayer and for Colgate.
Thompson said the joint venture made it difficult "to convince someone that this network with all these names on the door is a fully functioning agency."

With the alliance now disbanded, "it's cleared up for the outside world," he said, although noting that FCB has not had to face up to any major tests since then. "We haven't had any big pitches in the (last) four months," he said.

But despite the problems that surfaced during the joint venture's lifetime, Thompson said the alliance with Publicis made sense when it was formed because FCB at the time did not have a complete European network. "We felt it was better to hook up with Publicis than build from the ground up," he said. "It was the right decision at the time."
